description: Contributor-facing manifest of vetted Khmer-safe fonts. Phase 2b deliverable. Each entry documents a font that has been verified for self-hosting on the eInvite platform, including its OpenType shaping features for Khmer and its recommended line-height. The runtime font registry (window.EInviteFontRegistry) is generated from docs/typography-contract.json by src/python/generate_typography_contract.py; this manifest is the canonical, human-readable source for what SHOULD be in that contract. When adding a new font: append an entry here, mirror it into docs/typography-contract.json, drop the WOFF2 into assets/fonts/, record its SHA-256, then regenerate the contract.

add_new_font_checklist: Verify the font is OFL-1.1 (or another license that permits bundling + redistribution + embedding — MIT/Apache are also acceptable; proprietary fonts are NOT acceptable).

If the font supports Khmer, verify all 13 Noto Khmer OpenType shaping features are present (ccmp, akhn, pref, blwf, pstf, abvs, blws, psts, haln, liga, clig, kern, mark, mkmk). Run `ttx -t GSUB -t GPOS <font.woff2>` and check the FeatureList.
Record the SHA-256 of the WOFF2 file in BOTH this manifest (per-file `sha256` field) and `docs/typography-contract.json` (`assetSha256` block).
Record `name_en` AND `name_kh` (bilingual per ROADMAP ground rule 5). If a Khmer translation is not yet available, use the transliteration and tag the entry with `name_kh_pending: true`.
Mirror the entry into `docs/typography-contract.json` `fonts` block and re-run `python3 src/python/generate_typography_contract.py`.
Add a row to `docs/FONT_LICENSES_AND_REGISTRY.md` (V20 license inventory).
policy.khmer_safety_rule: A font with `supports_khmer: true` MUST be paired in every stack with at least one bundled Khmer-capable font as a fallback. The runtime font browser (src/js/font-browser.js) labels such fonts 'Khmer ready' or 'Khmer partial' accordingly. Fonts with `supports_khmer: false` are accepted ONLY when their stack includes 'Noto Sans Khmer' or 'Noto Serif Khmer' as a fallback.
policy.bilingual_label_rule: Every entry MUST have `name_en` and `name_kh`. The font browser UI (src/js/font-browser.js) renders the appropriate label based on the host's `languageMode` (English-only / Khmer-only / both) per ROADMAP ground rule 5.
